review.title: A variational symplectic scheme based on Lobatto's quadrature
review.summary: The paper presents a variational integrator derived from Lobatto's quadrature (a four-point rule exact for polynomials up to degree five) combined with cubic Lagrange interpolation. The discrete Lagrangian is constructed for the harmonic oscillator and the nonlinear pendulum, internal degrees of freedom are eliminated via discrete Euler–Lagrange equations, and the resulting one-step map is shown to be symplectic (unit determinant) and conditionally stable (hω < √(42−6√29) ≈ π). The scheme achieves sixth-order accuracy (superconvergence) for state, momentum, and energy in both test problems. Numerical results on the harmonic oscillator show near-exact energy conservation over 100,000 periods, and the nonlinear pendulum simulations confirm sixth-order convergence in the maximum norm.

strengths.point: Clear derivation of Lobatto's quadrature with explicit coefficients and proof of exactness for polynomials up to degree five.
strengths.quote: Lobatto's quadrature (\ref{eq:lobattoQuad}) is accurate for polynomials up to degree 2 n-3, where n is the number of integration points. In the present case n=4, so the proposed Lobatto quadrature is exact for the integration of polynomials up to degree five

strengths.point: Detailed construction of the discrete Lagrangian for the harmonic oscillator, including explicit elimination of internal degrees of freedom and a rigorous stability analysis yielding a conditional stability bound.
strengths.quote: The internal degrees of freedom q_ξ and q_{1-ξ} are eliminated by solving the system formed by the discrete Euler-Lagrange equations inside the interval, that is ∂L_d/∂q_ξ=0, ∂L_d/∂q_{1-ξ}=0. ... Δ < 0 when 0 < h ω < √(42-6√29). This restriction supersedes the previous stability condition ... Under this new restriction, two complex conjugate roots of unit module are obtained, guaranteeing numerical stability.

strengths.point: Sixth-order accuracy (superconvergence) demonstrated analytically for the harmonic oscillator and numerically for both the harmonic oscillator and the nonlinear pendulum, with tables showing the expected order of convergence for state, momentum, and energy.
strengths.quote: The method is symplectic and conditionally stable. It uses cubic Lagrange polynomials for its internal interpolation and results to be sixth-order accurate for the state, the momentum, and the system energy (twice the order of the selected polynomials). This superconvergence is a characteristic of Galerkin variational integrators as remarked in \cite{oberBlobaum2015,oberBlobaum2021}.

concerns.point: The claim that the method is 'conditionally stable' is only substantiated for the harmonic oscillator; no stability analysis is provided for the nonlinear pendulum, yet the conclusion states the method is conditionally stable in general.
concerns.quote: The method is symplectic and conditionally stable. ... Δ < 0 when 0 < h ω < √(42-6√29). ... The method remains stable by using a little more than two points per period of oscillation in this case.
concerns.suggestion: Either provide a stability analysis for the nonlinear pendulum or qualify the claim to apply only to the harmonic oscillator (or to linear systems).

concerns.point: The abstract states the method 'preserves an approximate energy quantity,' but a discrete preserved energy is only explicitly constructed for the harmonic oscillator (H_d). For the nonlinear pendulum, only energy error norms are reported, not a preserved discrete Hamiltonian.
concerns.quote: It preserves an approximate energy quantity. ... The method preserves a discrete Hamiltonian as remarked by \cite{benettin1994}.
concerns.suggestion: Clarify whether a discrete energy is exactly preserved for the nonlinear pendulum, or restrict the claim to the harmonic oscillator case.

withdrawn.point: The paper cites \cite{oberBlobaum2015} in the text (twice) but this reference is missing from the bibliography, making it impossible to verify the claimed prior publication of the harmonic oscillator scheme.
withdrawn.why: Checked in the LaTeX source by code: every reference has a label and every citation a bibliography entry.

The relationship between these parameters and how the nonlinear implicit equations are solved (e.g., Newton tolerance) is not given.
withdrawn.why: The concern incorrectly states that the nonlinear pendulum energy error figure uses 1e5 periods; the paper's Figure \ref{fig:errorEvolutionNL} caption explicitly says 5e3 periods.

questions: The stability analysis is only carried out for the harmonic oscillator; can the authors comment on the stability of the scheme for the nonlinear pendulum or for general nonlinear Hamiltonian systems?

The abstract claims the method 'preserves an approximate energy quantity.' For the nonlinear pendulum, is there a discrete energy that is exactly preserved by the map, or is the energy error merely observed to be small?

How are the implicit nonlinear equations for the pendulum solved in practice (e.g., Newton iteration, tolerance, initial guess), and what is the computational cost per step compared to the implicit midpoint or Simpson methods?

related.title: [0810.1548] Variational Integrators for Almost-Integrable Systems
related.note: Derives variational integrators using Gauss-Lobatto quadrature to approximate the action integral, showing the Lobatto coefficients arise naturally in the discrete Lagrangian framework.

related.title: Variational Integrators in Holonomic Mechanics
related.note: Shows Galerkin variational integrators based on Lobatto quadrature are equivalent to constrained Lobatto partitioned Runge-Kutta methods, confirming the variational-Lobatto connection for constrained systems.

related.title: Variational integrators for degenerate Lagrangians, with ...
related.note: Proves variational integrators from discrete Lagrangians are symplectic via discrete fiber derivatives and discrete Euler-Lagrange equations, the same theoretical structure used in the paper.

related.title: References
related.note: Presents a symplectic Simpson variational scheme for the harmonic oscillator with explicit discrete Hamiltonian and verified unit determinant, a different quadrature-based variational integrator.

related.title: Energy-preserving Variational Integrators for Forced ...
related.note: Constructs adaptive time-step variational integrators for forced Lagrangian systems using discrete Euler-Lagrange equations, demonstrating the same variational framework on a damped harmonic oscillator.

related.assessment: The paper's combination of Lobatto quadrature with cubic Lagrange interpolation to achieve sixth-order superconvergence for both state and energy appears novel; the search results confirm the variational-Lobatto framework is known, but not this specific quadrature-interpolation pairing or the conditional stability bound hω < √(42−6√29). The superconvergence claim for nonlinear pendulum and 100,000-period energy conservation could not be verified from snippets alone.

results.title: Symplectic P-stable additive Runge—Kutta methods
results.content: Classical symplectic partitioned Runge–Kutta methods can be obtained from a variational formulation where all the terms in the discrete Lagrangian are treated with the same quadrature formula. We construct a family of symplectic methods allowing the use of different quadrature formulas (primary and secondary) for different terms of the Lagrangian. In particular, we study a family of methods using Lobatto quadrature (with corresponding Lobatto IIIA-B symplectic pair) as a primary method and [...] primary method and Gauss–Legendre quadrature as a secondary method. The methods have the same implicitness as the underlying Lobatto IIIA-B pair, and, in addition, they are P-stable, therefore suitable for application to highly oscillatory problems.

Numerical algorithms based on variational and symplectic integrators exhibit special features that make them promising candidates for application to general relativity and other constrained Hamiltonian systems. This paper lays part of the foundation for such applications. The midpoint rule for Hamilton’s equations is examined from the perspectives of variational and symplectic integrators. It is shown that the midpoint rule preserves the symplectic form, conserves Noether charges, and exhibits [...] and exhibits excellent long-term energy behavior. The energy behavior is explained by the result, shown here, that the midpoint rule exactly conserves a phase space function that is close to the Hamiltonian.
